subject: giant eagle
title: A 33-Pound Eagle Killed Birds 13 Times Its Weight, and People May Have Been Next

scenes.text: The biggest eagle that ever lived killed prey thirteen times its own weight.
Haast's eagle of New Zealand. Fifteen kilograms, a three-metre wingspan, talons nine centimetres long.
It hunted moa, flightless birds weighing up to 200 kilograms. It knocked them over and struck the back of the neck.
Then it fed like a vulture, head deep inside the body. 3D scans in 2021 showed its skull was built like a condor's.
Maori cave art shows it with a bare head. Oral tradition says it hunted people too. An 80-kilo human is lighter than a moa.
When the moa were hunted out, about 700 years ago, the eagle starved. The only eagle that may have eaten us, gone.

description:
The biggest eagle that ever lived killed prey thirteen times its own weight.
Haast's eagle of New Zealand weighed about 15 kilograms with a wingspan of up to three metres and talons around nine centimetres long. It hunted moa, flightless birds of up to 200 kilograms, toppling them and striking the back of the neck, then fed like a vulture with its head inside the carcass; a 2021 study in Proceedings of the Royal Society B found its braincase resembled a condor's even though its beak and talons were an eagle's. Maori oral tradition suggests it also hunted people. It disappeared around 700 years ago, after the moa were hunted to extinction.
Would you rather face a Haast's eagle or a moa?
first_comment: DNA showed its closest living relative is the little eagle, which weighs about one kilogram. It grew fifteen times bigger in under two million years. Which extinct predator scares you most?
